## Role
Act as the kit `coordinator` in this session (read the bundled `coordinator` agent definition if this session was not started with it). Read `.harness/MEMORY.md` if present before anything else.

## Routing
Detect the input shape from $ARGUMENTS: free text proposes `discover`; a file path whose PRD-style `Status` table row starts with `aprovado`/`approved` (case-insensitive) proposes `plan`; a `PLAN.md` path with a sibling `PLAN.review.md` whose last round verdict is `approved` proposes `build`; any other file path proposes `discover`, same as free text. Before any file write or specialist dispatch, show the detected stage and ask the owner once, in a single numbered-prose message, for: (1) the confirmed or corrected start stage; (2) decision mode — (a) decide and record everything, (b) ask only product or contract decisions [default when unspecified], (c) ask every decision; (3) commit+push authorization; (4) pull-request authorization; (5) merge authorization; (6) tag authorization; (7) an eval spend cap in US$. There is no separate branch-per-slice question in this version. Persist the answers to a new `.harness/tasks/AUTO-<n>/BRIEF.md` and the same summary to `.harness/MEMORY.md` before dispatching the first stage; never write a file or dispatch a specialist before this questionnaire is answered.
In mode (a), decide and record every open decision yourself, including one a chained command's own Routing or Prerequisites text says to ask the owner (for example `discover.md`'s open questions or `build.md`'s Prerequisites); a plan already `approved` by document validation proceeds straight to `build` with no extra approval question. In mode (b), ask only a product or contract decision and auto-advance every other stage transition on its own. In mode (c), ask every decision mode (a) would otherwise take silently. In (b) or (c), before asking any decision question during execution, write the `Stage:` line and the `.harness/MEMORY.md` summary for the unit in progress first, so `/dh:resume` can continue the run even if the session ends before the owner answers.
Regardless of decision mode, stop the run immediately, with no exception, on any of: a demonstrated vulnerability or a confirmed exposure (a hypothesis alone does not stop the run); a destructive action or one touching real data; an unauthorized dependency install; the eval spend cap from the questionnaire being reached; the applicable round cap exhausted — name which one, since this chain can hit either: two rounds for document validation, six for build, QA or code review; a paid eval case's judge score in that run's result JSON below the pass bar the plan fixed for that case before any paid run; a rule conflict that would change the shape of the delivery. On any stop, write the exact state and the pending decision to `.harness/MEMORY.md` and end the run — no wait loop, no automatic retry; `/dh:resume` continues from the `Stage:` line below. At the six-round build/QA/review cap specifically, this command does not itself replan: it records the blocked state with `Stage:` at the interrupted unit and ends, and replanning with the owner happens in a later session, per `coordinator.md` Procedure item 8, never inline here.
After each completed stage, report one status line — stage, verdict, next stage — and update the matching `.harness/MEMORY.md` entry at the same time. Follow each chained command's own Routing and Prerequisites text inline, never re-invoking it as a separate slash command, inheriting whatever review depth and correction cap it already states rather than imposing a new one. `build`'s QA and independent code review run exactly as `build.md` requires: frozen state, six-round cap, unchanged. Document review at the PRD stage (`discover.md`) and the PLAN stage (`plan.md`) both cap at two correction rounds under the lean proportionality rule in `coordinator.md` ("Proportional review and paid evaluation"): one reviewer from the configured list by default, the full panel only when the owner asks for it in this run or the document touches security. `discover.md`'s PRD-stage dispatch is conditional on `reviewers.document`; `plan.md`'s PLAN-stage dispatch is unconditional (always `document-validator`) — a pre-existing asymmetry this command does not resolve, since in the common case (`reviewers.document` absent, or listing `claude`) both stages already behave identically. This command asks no open question beyond the questionnaire and the hard stops above, so the owner-ask panel trigger fires in practice only when the owner names it inside the questionnaire's free-form context or a mode-(b)/(c) decision question, never as a separate question this command adds.
After each slice's build gates (QA and code review) pass and before the next slice starts, run `secure.md`'s own trigger verbatim — no authentication, data, input or execution surface — never a narrower list of this command's own invention; dispatch `security-reviewer` exactly as `secure.md` describes when the trigger surface is touched, otherwise record one skip for that slice with the reason. Run `/dh:review`'s procedure once, after the whole slice loop completes, before `release`.
Create a single `<base-branch>` from `main` at the start of the run and use it for the whole batch; no per-slice branch. The batch's one closing commit happens only with commit+push authorization (3); the one pull request targeting `main` happens only with pull-request authorization (4).
Before every paid eval run in this batch, check: spent so far (agent cost plus judge cost of every run already completed in this batch) + this run's `--max-cost-usd` + this run's estimated judge cost <= the questionnaire's US$ cap. Estimate the judge cost from the last recorded baseline's judge/agent cost ratio for that case, multiplied by `--max-cost-usd`; with no recorded baseline, the estimate equals `--max-cost-usd` itself. Exceeding the inequality is the hard stop "eval spend cap reached": the paid run does not start.
Persist run state at `.harness/tasks/AUTO-<n>/BRIEF.md`. Its `Stage:` line always names the next unit to execute — a chain stage, a slice, or, inside the git sequence below, the step name `commit`, `proof`, `push`, `pr`, `merge` or `tag`. Completing a unit advances `Stage:` to the next one; a stop leaves `Stage:` naming the interrupted unit, never marked complete. A stop inside the git sequence specifically writes that sequence's own interrupted step name into `Stage:`, never a generic `release` marker.
Read and follow `.commands/release.md`'s Routing, Prerequisites, Output and Limits text inline, in this same session, never invoking `/dh:release` as a separate slash command — its `disable-model-invocation` field blocks only that separate invocation, not this command reading its text.
Enter the git sequence only once `release`'s procedure reports ready for decision; otherwise the run ends per the stop behavior above with `Stage: release` recorded. In order, run only the steps the questionnaire authorized: (1) commit — the batch's one closing commit, only with authorization (3); (2) clean-clone sha256 reproducibility proof, only when that commit regenerated `dist/`, run before push — `amend` is allowed only while the commit stays unpushed, never `--force`; (3) push, only after the proof (when applicable) passes; (4) open a pull request to `main`, only with authorization (4); (5) merge, only with authorization (5) AND a green CI (a pending CI may be awaited; red, off or broken CI ends the run instead, with state recorded) AND the independent in-session code-review verdict `approve` already recorded in `.harness/MEMORY.md` — never a GitHub PR review state — using the project's usual squash; (6) tag, only with authorization (6), after step (5)'s merge, on the merge or squash commit. A step without its authorization ends the run at that point with the state recorded; withholding merge authorization (5) leaves an opened pull request open, never auto-merged. Never `--force` or `--no-verify` anywhere in this sequence.
Dispatch only roles already under `.agents/` and skills already under `.skills/`, plus whatever `cli:...` entries `.harness/project.yaml`'s `reviewers:` already configures. This command adds no new agent, skill or role of its own.

## Prerequisites
$ARGUMENTS: an idea, a PRD path, or a `PLAN.md` path; free text with no recognizable path is treated as an idea. `.harness/project.yaml`, read once at the start of the run, for `reviewers:` and check commands. The owner must answer the seven-item questionnaire before the first stage starts; unlike a low-stakes intake question elsewhere in this kit, there is no unattended default answer for it.

## Output
One status line per completed stage (stage, verdict, next stage), the running `.harness/tasks/AUTO-<n>/BRIEF.md` record (questionnaire answers, current `Stage:`), and, when the run reaches publication, the merged pull-request link and the pushed tag. Each chained stage's own output — the `incremental-implementation` report, the QA matrix, the review findings, the `delivery-readiness` package — is produced exactly as that stage's own command already defines and is not restated here.

## Limits
- Every restriction of the chained command currently running applies unreduced: this command loosens no gate, cap or authorization check any `.commands/<stage>.md` already states.
- The seven-item questionnaire runs exactly once per run, before the first write or dispatch; a later stage's own "ask the owner" text is answered per the active decision mode, never by re-running the questionnaire.
- No branch other than the single `<base-branch>` for the whole batch; no per-slice branch.
- No git-sequence step without its own questionnaire letter; no `--force`, no `--no-verify`.
- No new agent, skill or role beyond what `.agents/` and `.skills/` already define.
- Only the Coordinator writes `.harness/MEMORY.md`, `EPOCHAL.md` and `RISKS.md`.

## Next
`/dh:resume` to continue an interrupted run from its `Stage:` line.
